attacks.claim: The zone fill is the highest of the three band ratings, a derived summary the issuing center did not publish. The WADE agreement says ratings may not be altered, and the artifact says ratings are shown exactly as issued. Nothing shows legal or WADE approved this aggregation. LGL-902 covered only the card text and terms update.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three" vs. "may not alter ratings or forecast text" and "We show the rating exactly as issued"

attacks.claim: The expiry rule covers only the zone fill and label. The card contents and the VoiceOver/TalkBack output for expired or no-forecast zones are unspecified, and QA checked only the visual gray state. A screen-reader user or a card could still present band ratings as current, against the agreed rule never to present stale safety information as current.
attacks.evidence: "zone announced as \"[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]\"" and "the card lists all three bands with their ratings"; ABSENT: card and screen-reader behavior for expired zones

attacks.claim: A center asking to stop display cannot be honored on devices. Its offline copies keep showing color until each forecast's valid_until. Per-center purge of offline data does not exist. Flag-off reaches only devices that fetch remote config on foreground, and the rollback text (next foreground) conflicts with the QA row (next launch). The 'no stale ratings remain' claim is therefore not established for the withdrawal case.
attacks.evidence: "its zones disappear within 10 min and any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`" vs. "takes effect on next app foreground" and QA "purged on next launch"

attacks.claim: The free-form `bbox` on an unauthenticated endpoint has no stated validation, maximum extent, or cache-key normalization. This risks large payloads and cache fragmentation, so the 92% hit rate and the cost estimate are unsupported. No load test was run, and CDN spend has only an alert.
attacks.evidence: `GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…` ... "CDN budget alert at $400/month"; ABSENT: bbox limits, load test

attacks.claim: The offline clock guard catches only a clock set earlier than the download time. A clock set back to a value between download time and real time keeps an expired forecast in color. The CDN TTL is also unstated, though the on-device valid_until check mitigates it.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired"; ABSENT: CDN TTL

attacks.claim: The flag goes to 100% at 08:00 but the check that all 19 centers render happens only before the 10:00 blog post, so users see the layer for two hours unchecked. The check has no defined criteria or owner, and the blog post has no correction path if the set of centers changes.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%. Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check that all 19 centers render."

attacks.claim: The gray hatched state has no legend entry and does not distinguish expired from no-forecast zones. Time format and time zone for the issue and valid-until times are unspecified.
attacks.evidence: "the legend lists all five levels with names"; ABSENT: time zone and format

attacks.claim: The bbox plus IP in origin logs reveals approximate viewed areas. Log retention and analytics identifier and consent handling are unstated.
attacks.evidence: "device location is not sent"; ABSENT: retention, consent handling
